t: You're on Fleet Street, the old road that runs from Temple Bar, where the City of London meets Westminster, down to Ludgate Circus. It takes its name from the River Fleet, which once ran here. Several people have their story tied to this street. Mary Frith, known as Moll Cutpurse, a notorious pickpocket and fence of the London underworld, died here in 1659. John Bowyer Nichols, a printer and antiquarian, was born on this street. The photographer James Edward Ellam died here, and the writer Francis Charles Laird lived here.
